topic: Complex Conditional Pointer Checks with Side-Effect-Free Operations
explanation: In advanced C programming, it is often necessary to perform conditional pointer checks combined with side-effect-free operations such as casting or function calls that do not alter program state. This technique ensures safe dereferencing and conditional execution while maintaining code clarity and avoiding unintended side effects, especially in performance-critical or low-level code. It demonstrates careful handling of pointers and conditional logic to prevent undefined behavior and improve robustness.
